subsystems.name: Vacuum and atom source
subsystems.role: provides an ultra-high-vacuum environment and a supply of cold atoms.

subsystems.name: Optical tweezer array
subsystems.role: creates hundreds of tightly focused laser spots, each trapping one atom.
parts: spatial light modulator or acousto-optic deflectors

subsystems.name: Laser cooling system
subsystems.role: slows atoms to microkelvin temperatures so they can be captured.

subsystems.name: Rydberg excitation
subsystems.role: promotes atoms to giant Rydberg states so neighbouring atoms interact strongly and switchably.

subsystems.name: Readout
subsystems.role: reports which sites hold an atom and what state it is in.

subsystems.name: Classical control
subsystems.role: sequences laser pulses in time and analyses the results.

buildSteps.title: Build the vacuum cell
buildSteps.detail: A glass cell and chamber are assembled and baked to ultra-high vacuum, so atoms travel far without colliding with background gas.

buildSteps.title: Load and cool atoms
buildSteps.detail: A magneto-optical trap collects a cloud of atoms and laser light cools it to a few microkelvin above absolute zero.

buildSteps.title: Form the tweezer array
buildSteps.detail: One laser beam is split by a spatial light modulator into a grid of foci, each less than a micrometre wide, focused through a high-numerical-aperture objective.

buildSteps.title: Trap single atoms
buildSteps.detail: The cold cloud is overlapped with the array so one atom settles in each focus; light-assisted collisions eject atoms from doubly occupied sites, leaving one per tweezer.

buildSteps.title: Rearrange into a perfect pattern
buildSteps.detail: Tweezers are moved to shuffle atoms along, filling gaps so the array is defect-free before computation begins.

buildSteps.title: Encode and manipulate qubits
buildSteps.detail: Atoms are prepared in chosen internal states; laser pulses entangle neighbours, and Rydberg blockade makes that interaction switchable site by site.

buildSteps.title: Read out
buildSteps.detail: A laser drives fluorescence from occupied sites, and a camera records which atoms survived and in which state.

buildSteps.title: Scale and connect
buildSteps.detail: Arrays are extended to more sites with better optics and vacuum, and photonic links are added to entangle separate arrays.

prerequisites.why: only microkelvin atoms can be held in a tweezer for long enough to compute.
they confine a single atom in a spot smaller than a micrometre.
it supplies strong, switchable interactions between neighbouring atoms.

prerequisites.tech: Spatial light modulators and fast control electronics
prerequisites.why: hundreds of beams must be shaped and steered within microseconds.
logical qubits require errors to be detected and fixed while the computation continues.
one optical system is finite in size; linking modules is the route to much larger machines.

pathway.milestone: arrays of a few hundred atoms used as analog simulators and small digital processors
pathway.unlocks: research on quantum many-body physics and first error-correction experiments.

pathway.milestone: thousands of atoms with real-time measurement and correction
pathway.unlocks: logical qubits that outlive the physical atoms making them up.

pathway.milestone: modular machines linked by photonic entanglement
pathway.unlocks: scaling past the limit of a single array and objective.
applications in chemistry, materials and optimisation.
